Last Sphinx artifact and receipt retained and proven redeployable after source removal
Sweep: no remaining references to sphinx, furo, ablog, myst_parser, landing/shared, docs/_build in maintained code, workflows or Makefiles (grep output in PR)

description:
Start only when there is evidence (owner decision 2026-10-04: no elapsed-time window):
- at least one successful production deploy since the astro-site-53 cutover for each route class (stable docs from a release tag, dev docs, blog, and a results/corpus update), each with green public probes on every route
- the exact-artifact rollback drill evidence from astro-site-53 is on record, and a fresh drill on the current artifact passes
- the latest receipt shows every actively served route rendered by Astro
- the D14 agreements on overlapping items are honoured

Keep a deployable rollback target: the last Sphinx-rendered artifact and its receipt stay retained and redeployable after the source tooling is deleted, at least until the next release after retirement; the owner may extend this.

Then remove:
- docs/conf.py, docs/_extensions, docs/_templates, docs/Makefile, make.bat, the Sphinx-only parts of docs/_static
- landing/ and landing/shared
- Sphinx targets in make/documentation.mk and Makefile ci-docs, plus make/inventory.json entries
- the pyproject docs extra and the docs entries in the dev group (sphinx, furo, myst-parser, sphinxcontrib-mermaid, sphinx-tags, sphinx-design, ablog and its git source override)
- the Sphinx build from required CI, with its drift guard updated in the same PR
- redundant token-drift scripts
- Sphinx-specific tests, each replaced by its Astro equivalent

docs/ stays the content directory. Separately decide whether to rewrite the remaining MyST constructs to plain Markdown and retire the converter; if yes, record it as a follow-up item.
